cues: Stanza seven turns from witnessing to reflecting, and opens with the poem's one plainly hopeful image: crocuses have grown over the stone, I saw last moonlit night.
The flowers really have come up through the rock, placed right after the worst stanzas.
Then storms loiter in the narrow lanes, hanging about with no purpose, like the violence did.
And the crescendo: the storm rages over silent pages, silent stones, silent shirts, and the silent ruins of the gods' temples.
An enormous grief, and total silence.
